summary: A superconducting flux qubit network (10 qubits) coupled to a low-dissipation hybrid resonator exhibits Bose-Einstein condensation of microwave photons and collective Bogoliubov-like excitations observed via two-tone spectroscopy. The system displays bistability and hysteresis in photon occupancy as a function of pump power, with theory based on a nonlinear Gross-Pitaevskii-type equation quantitatively reproducing the experimental transmission spectra.
motivation: Josephson junction networks coupled to high-quality resonators can exhibit macroscopic collective quantum dynamics and strong photon-photon interactions via the ac Stark effect, enabling exploration of nonlinear photon physics and potential applications in quantum sensing.
method: Two-tone spectroscopy measured transmission $|S_{21}(f)|$ through a T-resonator ($f_r \approx 7.7$ GHz, $Q_c \approx 10^5$) while a pump field at variable power $P_{\mathrm{pump}}$ and frequency populated the coupled R-resonator, with a probe beam scanning resonances. The system operated at 15 mK with applied static magnetic field $B$ up to 0.489 G. Theoretical analysis employed a semiclassical nonlinear Schrödinger equation with ac Stark-induced photon nonlinearity of the form $1+4g_j^2|\psi|^2/\Delta_j^2$.
result: Sharp abrupt frequency shift of the resonant transmission dip occurred above critical pump power $P_{\mathrm{cr}}$ within a narrow pump frequency window ($7.743$–$7.746$ GHz), accompanied by hysteresis loops and emergence of idler resonances. Fitted parameters: $g/2\pi \approx 25$ MHz, $\Delta/2\pi \approx 1.78$ GHz, cavity decay $\gamma_c/2\pi \approx 3.2$ MHz; magnetic field tuning shifted $P_{\mathrm{cr}}$ downward and modified resonant positions by $\approx 0.2$ MHz/G in qubit frequency.
